verdicts.summary: Reproduced on the local DB for 2018-01-01..2025-03-24. R2 share is 47.7% with the fixed-100 gate and 23.3% with the adaptive gate; the two disagree on 30.1% of 1,816 sessions. SignalEngine's VVIX>100 override turned precomputed adaptive labels into a union with 50.8% R2, and only 72.6% of rows equalled label.shift(1). VVIX=100 is the 67.6th percentile over 2010-2026 and the 52.0th over the backtest window. Persistence 2020-2025 is 0.8998 on fixed labels and 0.866 on adaptive labels. Fix: regime_classifier now has one gate definition, R2_GATE (None = adaptive) plus r2_gate_threshold() and r2_gate_state(). It is the default of build_regime_labels, build_dataset, train_classifier, RegimePipeline and regime_label_noise_audit; the backtest picks it up through the default. The hard-coded override in SignalEngine.generate is removed. Precomputed labels are reindexed to sessions and lagged by one session, never modified. The classifier research path takes R2 from the canonical rule. regime_label_summary() gives shares and persistence on the labels actually used (adaptive 2020-2025: 86.7%). The '75th percentile' docstring is corrected. Code side of docs-regime-gate-backtest-vs-site is covered here.
verdicts.tests: test_regime_classifier.py::TestR2Gate (default_gate_is_adaptive, r2_exactly_where_gate_state_is_on, missing_vvix_print_does_not_fail_open, vvix_outage_leaves_label_unknown, label_summary_persistence); TestLabelNoiseAudit::test_audits_the_labels_actually_used; test_signal_engine.py::TestPrecomputedRegimesAreOnlyLagged (2 tests), TestSignalEngineGenerate::test_default_regimes_are_lagged_canonical_rule_labels; test_lookahead.py::TestSignalEngineLags::test_regime_is_previous_session_label. Mutations caught: re-adding the VVIX>100 override; making fixed 100 the default.

verdicts.summary: Code side only. Verified the same divergence as signals-r2-gate-adaptive-vs-fixed: backtest regime = fixed-100 labels shifted one session; site labels = adaptive. Now one gate (adaptive) is used everywhere, so the site caption 'the label the backtest trades on' becomes true once the backtest is rerun. The texts that must change (Step 5 numbers, 90.0% persistence, README C13) are in published_number_changes and cross_chain_requests.

Reproduced on the canonical signals: mean WF-PDV σ̂ 0.118 vs mean forward RV21 0.167 (ratio 0.705; √(2/π)=0.798); pdv_iv_spread mean −8.01 vp; P(spread<−0.02 | R1)=0.965. The model change belongs to the PDV chain and is not implemented here. Signal side: build_features(pdv_vol_series=...) is now the documented injection hook, with the contract annualised decimal σ at the VIX horizon (~21 sessions), dated ≤ t. Inputs are validated: date index, duplicates keep last, vol points (median>3) and negative values raise ValueError. Provenance goes to .attrs['pdv_iv_spread_source'] and proxy-filled days are counted in .attrs['pdv_iv_spread_n_proxy']. SignalEngine.generate(precomputed_pdv_vol=...) passes it through. The 'IVR' misnomer is removed from my code and docstrings, including the signal_summary key.

Reproduced: all 8 S2 stops in 2018-2025 fired on favourable moves, for example 2019-09-16, a short stopped as VIX fell from 15.00 to 13.74. The stop is now expressed in the straddle actually traded: adverse = −position × (VIX_t/VIX_entry − 1) > 15%. Long straddles stop when front vol falls and shorts when it rises. The logic is shared by S2 and S2X (_apply_s2_stop), and s2_stop / s2x_stop columns flag stop sessions. Effect in the canonical run, on top of the gate fix: S2 −44,397 → −87,706 (S2 is not in NAV). The old test encoded the inverted direction and was rewritten. Mirror cases cover both sides.
verdicts.tests: test_signal_engine.py::TestGenerateSignal2: long_straddle_stopped_when_front_vol_falls (checks propagation until the next entry), long_not_stopped_when_front_vol_rises, short_stopped_when_front_vol_rises, short_not_stopped_when_front_vol_falls, small_adverse_move_does_not_stop, r2exit_variant_uses_same_stop. Mutation M15 (sign flip) caught.

verdicts.summary: Reproduced: 1,816 SPX sessions but 1,808 backtest rows, and the 8 missing sessions each follow a NaN VVIX. NaN-VVIX days were labelled R1 because NaN > x is False (fails open), for example 2020-06-11. Fix: fill_vvix carries one missing print forward (VVIX_FFILL_LIMIT=1, causal) in both build_features and the gate. A longer outage, or the adaptive gate's 63-print warm-up, makes the label unknown rather than R1. SignalEngine keeps every session with a known lagged regime; a NaN input only silences the signals that read it. Effect in the canonical run: rows 1,808 → 1,816; NAV 738,794 → 739,833 with the fixed gate. Adaptive labels change on 1 day (2021-05-20: 1→2) and fixed-100 labels on 7 days.
verdicts.tests: test_regime_classifier.py::TestBuildFeatures::test_vvix_missing_print_carried_one_session, TestR2Gate::test_missing_vvix_print_does_not_fail_open, ::test_vvix_outage_leaves_label_unknown; test_signal_engine.py::TestSessionsSurviveMissingVVIX::test_every_session_is_kept (one missing print, a two-day outage and a missing VIX3M). Mutations caught: no VVIX fill; dropping NaN sessions.

verdicts.summary: Verified that the old tests poisoned data strictly after the cutoff and compared positions only, and that several assertions were vacuous ('or True'; an S3 max-hold test that never opened a position; a len() check). New test_lookahead.py Category 5: (a) same-day poison: two opposite poisons at four cutoffs where the lagged regime is R1, requiring every numeric column ≤ t to be identical, including s2/s3/s4 z-scores, features and regime; (b) explicit feature-lag and regime-lag checks; (c) label and adaptive-gate causality for both gates, plus a non-vacuity check; (d) HMM truncation invariance and a hand-set model on which full-sequence decoding would differ. SignalEngine now outputs s2_z, s3_z and s4_z so the tests can compare them. Vacuous tests in test_signal_engine and test_regime_classifier were replaced with real expectations. Mutation testing on a scratch copy: 17 of 17 caught — no feature lag, no regime lag, full-sample S3 z, VVIX shift(-1), centred gate, rv using r(t+1), HMM smoothing, HMM Viterbi, HMM VIX ordering, VVIX>100 override, flipped S2 stop, band-only S1 exit, no VVIX fill, fixed-100 default, window-first stats, in-sample calibrator, dropping NaN sessions.
verdicts.tests: test_lookahead.py::TestSignalEngineSameDayPoison (8 parametrised), TestSignalEngineLags (3), TestRegimeLabelCausality (6), TestHMMIsFiltered (2); test_regime_classifier.py::TestBuildFeatures::test_no_future_data_used (now a poison test); test_signal_engine.py S1/S2/S3 max-hold and entry tests made non-vacuous.

verdicts.summary: Reproduced: 22 sign flips of pdv_iv_spread in the canonical signals, 10 of which skip the ±0.5 vp band (median daily move 0.55 vp). Exits for S1, S1C and S1X are now keyed to the entry side: a trade entered on a positive spread exits once the spread is below +0.5 vp, and one entered on a negative spread once it is above −0.5 vp. This required optional exit_long / exit_short arguments on both state machines. Effect after the gate fix: S1 +1,901,525 → +1,930,331, S1C −1,304,732 → −1,323,402, NAV 480,833 → 474,609.

Code side. Verified that RegimePipeline loaded the full-sample pdv_model.pkl (look-ahead) and that 63.4%, 86.2% and 90.0% are string literals no code computes. Added classifier_accuracy_report(): lagged features, injected walk-forward σ̂ or the rv proxy (never pdv_model.pkl), canonical gate, single split, per-year walk-forward and benchmarks, each with persistence on the same rows. evaluate_classifier gained provenance keys and a previous-session persistence option. RegimePipeline no longer loads pdv_model.pkl by default. The 'circular vvix' comment is corrected: vvix(t−1) is a legitimate lagged predictor. Results on adaptive labels, rv proxy, 2010-2019 → 2020-01-02..2025-12-31 (1,488 rows): in-sample 78.7%, OOS 75.1%, per-year walk-forward 75.1%, persistence 86.8%. With vvix: 72.3% OOS. With vvix plus y(t−1): 83.1% OOS. With WF-PDV features: OOS 76.6%, walk-forward 73.5%. The demotion stands. Fixed-100 labels give OOS 52.6% vs persistence 91.1%. The shipped pickle is retrained and stores this evaluation in metadata_.

Code side: accuracy is now computed (classifier_accuracy_report) and recorded in the shipped pickle as metadata_['evaluation'] (oos_acc 0.751, persistence_acc 0.868, n_test 1488, ECE). The dashboard's hard-coded '63.4%' and its live-inference ordering bug, where pdv_forecast is read before the PDV block sets it, are in dashboard/app.py, which I do not own. Both are listed in cross_chain_requests.

Reproduced: CalibratedClassifierCV(FrozenEstimator) was fit on the booster's own training rows with balanced weights. On adaptive labels, 2020-2025, P(R2) ECE went from 0.150 raw to 0.177 and log-loss from 0.68 to 1.09; on fixed labels ECE went 0.127 → 0.175. A time-later holdout calibrator gives 0.042 (adaptive). Fix: RegimeClassifier.fit(calibration=None|'holdout') fits the booster on the earlier 80% of time-ordered rows and an unweighted one-vs-rest isotonic map on the later 20% it never saw. The map is stored as plain arrays. The default is None (raw booster output, documented as not calibrated); the shipped model uses 'holdout': OOS P(R2) ECE 0.150 → 0.031, Brier 0.177 → 0.139. The pickle is version-robust (booster JSON, no sklearn objects) and legacy pickles still load. This also removes a hard import of sklearn.frozen, which needs sklearn ≥1.6 while requirements allow ≥1.3.
verdicts.tests: test_regime_classifier.py::TestProbabilityCalibration (holdout_calibrator_sees_only_later_unseen_rows, holdout_calibration_improves_out_of_sample_ece, rejects_unknown_calibration), TestRegimeClassifier::test_default_fit_returns_raw_booster_probabilities, TestVersionRobustPickle (pickle_holds_no_sklearn_objects, legacy_wrapped_model_state_still_loads, shipped_classifier...). Mutation (calibrator on training rows) caught.

verdicts.summary: Reproduced on fixed labels: P(fwd RV>VIX) R0 0.144, R1 0.160, R2 0.161. On the canonical adaptive labels, 2010-2025: R0 0.189, R1 0.153, R2 0.171, with mean forward gaps −3.3 / −3.5 / −4.0 vp. So after R0 days forward RV still ends below VIX 81% of the time and the premise remains unsupported. Mean VIX: R0 0.187 > R1 0.167. Backwardation share: R0 4.4%, R1 1.0%, R2 28.9%. Docstrings in regime_classifier and signal_engine now describe R0/R1 as descriptive trailing states, with these numbers. Added regime_forward_premium_table() so the premise can be checked on any run; RegimePipeline.run includes it. The live-site legend fix is a dashboard request.

Verified: predict() used Viterbi and predict_proba_raw() used score_samples (forward-backward). On synthetic data the truncation difference in P was up to 0.69 with the old code. The mapping ranked states by mean VIX, but under the rule R1 has the lowest mean VIX, so R0 and R1 were swapped. Fix: forward-filtered posteriors (_forward_filter with emission log-pdfs; NaN rows get a predict-only step); predict() is the argmax of the filtered posterior. Mapping is map_states_to_regimes(): highest vvix → R2, lower fear_premium → R0. n_components must be 3. New defect fixed in the same area: single-start EM collapsed two states onto the same means on 2010-2019 data (log-likelihood 14,129). n_init=5 restarts reach 15,271 with three distinct states.
verdicts.tests: test_lookahead.py::TestHMMIsFiltered (truncation_invariance, labels_do_not_use_later_observations); test_regime_classifier.py::TestHMMRegimeClassifier (state_mapping_follows_rule_semantics, fit_uses_rule_semantic_mapping, requires_three_components, multi_start_fit_separates_distinct_clusters). Mutations caught: smoothing, Viterbi, VIX ordering.

verdicts.summary: Verified in the shipped DB: the row dated 2020-03-16 has vix_level 57.83, which is 2020-03-13's VIX (actual 82.69). The writer stored rv_20d = vix − spread = 2·VIX − RV and classifier predictions labelled 'regime'. The writer now uses regime_label_db_rows(build_rule_label_frame(...)): the rule label, same-day VIX and slope, the label's own rv_20d, and confidence 1.0 for the deterministic rule. RegimePipeline.run writes rule labels. The shipped vol_system.db is not mine and is not regenerated; a request is in cross_chain_requests.

Grep of the whole repo (joint_vol_calibration, dashboard, scripts, .github, shell scripts) found no reader. The signals file covered 2018-01-02..2025-03-24 with no s1c/s4 columns; the IVR panel had spread = VIX − PDV (opposite sign) and no producer. Both were deleted (git rm). SignalEngine.save() now defaults to default_signals_path(df), named after the span actually saved. SIGNALS_PATH was removed; only save() used it.

Partly overstated. The module docstring did not say that a single signal gives 0; it omitted the single-signal case. The function docstring was wrong about combined_pos (it is direction × weight, not × strength). Both docstrings now match the code; the equal half-weight for one versus two agreeing signals is documented rather than changed (research-only curve). On S3's sign, the entry thesis, the backtest's Δz P&L proxy and the combiner all treat +1 as the ratio reverting up, i.e. long index vol relative to VVIX. Only the 'long dispersion (short index vol)' docstring contradicted that and it is corrected. combined_kelly now caps at max(S1, S3, S4) via a new max_kelly argument instead of a hard-coded S1–S3 maximum and 0.20 (no numeric change today).

Verified with the new code: BacktestEngine().run() (loads from 2010) vs run_backtest (DATA_START 2015) differ only in S1 (81 days) and S1C (33 days) from 2018-12-27; S2, S3, S4 and regime are identical. The cause is the walk-forward PDV training on all pre-year history loaded. My warm-statistics fix made S2/S3/S4 independent of load start. The remaining fix (training window inside BacktestEngine) and the stale narrative numbers are in backtest_engine.py, run_backtest.py and the docs, which I do not own. See cross_chain_requests.

Verified: _build_walkforward_regimes has no caller, and run() always passes precomputed_regimes, so the classifier retrained in walk_forward_validation has no effect. _retrain_classifier fits unshifted X(t) → y(t). All of this is in backtest_engine.py (not mine); a request is in cross_chain_requests. Note: _retrain_classifier still works with the new RegimeClassifier.fit, because it reindexes X to y.

new_findings.description: SignalEngine.generate cut the features to [start, end] before the signals computed their 252-day trailing z-scores, so S2/S3/S4 statistics warmed up inside the backtest window. In 2018-01-02..2018-07-02 S3 and S4 never traded and S2 traded once, including Feb-2018, even though run_backtest loads from 2015 'so signal rolling windows are warm by 2018'. The S3 entry z also differed from the backtest's full-history S3 P&L z. Fix: statistics use all supplied history; entries are allowed only inside the window (new entry_allowed argument on the state machines and generators), so the book starts flat. Canonical effect after the other fixes: NAV 474,609 → 444,614; S2 −87,706 → −96,587; S3 +24,190 → +29,008; S4 −276,563 → −371,367.

save_regime_labels defaulted to LABELS_PARQUET (data_store/signals/regime_labels.parquet), so RegimePipeline.run() overwrote the shipped RULE labels with the demoted classifier's PREDICTIONS. That is the same class of bug C21 fixed in cloud_refresh. It now writes regime_classifier_predictions.parquet (columns pred_regime / pred_regime_name) and refuses the rule-label path.

regime_classifier imported sklearn.frozen.FrozenEstimator at module level. That class exists only in sklearn ≥1.6, while requirements.txt allows ≥1.3, so on 1.3–1.5 the signal engine, backtest and dashboard could not import the module, and the shipped pickle could not be unpickled. The import is removed and the pickle is re-saved in a format with no sklearn objects.

HMMRegimeClassifier.fit used a single EM start (seed 42). On 2010-2019 features it converged to a local optimum with two of three states on the same means (log-likelihood 14,129 vs 15,271 from other starts). Fixed with n_init=5 restarts, keeping the best log-likelihood. Even with distinct states, the filtered HMM labels match the rule labels on only ~28% of 2020-2025 sessions; this is now documented.

During the adaptive gate's first 62 VVIX prints the gate was NaN, and vvix > NaN silently meant 'not R2', so labels were assigned with no gate at all (47 sessions 2010-01-26..2010-04-02 in the shipped history, and the start of any short data load). These sessions are now unlabelled (gate unknown), and the signal engine carries the last known label.

SignalEngine lagged precomputed_regimes with .shift(1) on their own index. If the labels missed a session, the lag moved by position, not by session. Labels are now reindexed to the session calendar before the one-session lag, and duplicate dates are dropped.

evaluate_classifier computed persistence as the previous ROW of y_test. Rows dropped for NaN features made 'yesterday' two sessions back. It now optionally uses the previous labelled session (labels=...). regime_label_noise_audit's persistence also counted a spurious first comparison (NaN == x) and now uses regime_label_summary.

test_backtest_engine.py::TestEdgeCases::test_all_regime2_no_s1_entries sets VVIX = 150 constant and expects 'all Regime 2'. Under the canonical adaptive gate, a constant VVIX is never above its own trailing 80th percentile, so this is an intended behaviour change, not a regression. It is the only failing test in the full suite. A rising VVIX path (np.linspace(80, 200, n)) gives 100% R2 and 0% combined activity. File not owned; see cross_chain_requests.

cross_chain_requests.request: TestEdgeCases.test_all_regime2_no_s1_entries (line ~509): replace `vix["^VVIX"] = 150.0` with a strictly rising path, e.g. `vix["^VVIX"] = np.linspace(80.0, 200.0, len(vix))`. Reason: the canonical R2 gate is now the adaptive 252-session 80th percentile, and a constant VVIX is never above its own trailing percentile, so the current fixture yields 86% combined activity and fails. Verified: with the rising path every labelled session is R2 and combined activity is 0.0. Also update the docstring to 'VVIX above its trailing 80th percentile'. Note that the first 63 sessions now have no label (gate warm-up) and are dropped from the signal frame.

(1) Module docstring item 4, the ASSUMPTIONS strings at lines ~566-567 and ~591-593, and the run() comment at ~929: replace 'VVIX>100 → R2', '90.0% vs 63.4%' and '86.2%' with the adaptive gate (regime_classifier.R2_GATE, gate_name()) and computed numbers. Use regime_label_summary(labels, '2020-01-01', '2025-12-31')['persistence_acc'] = 0.867, and classifier_accuracy_report() or RegimeClassifier.load().metadata_['evaluation'] (OOS 0.751 vs persistence 0.868). (2) _build_walkforward_pdv_vol: switch to the PDV chain's horizon-21 variance-consistent σ forecast, passed unchanged through SignalEngine.generate(precomputed_pdv_vol=...); build_features validates it. (3) Make the WF-PDV training window independent of how much history the caller loads: BacktestEngine().run() vs run_backtest differ on S1 81 days and S1C 33 days from 2018-12-27; everything else is now identical. (4) Delete _build_walkforward_regimes and _retrain_classifier, which are dead and unshifted, and correct the walk_forward_validation docstring. (5) _build_s3_zscore docstring claims it 'matches generate_signal3 exactly'. The signal's decision z is now exposed as sig_df['s3_z'] and is lagged one session; the P&L z is same-day. Reword the claim. (6) The variants table can now use real simulations: sig_df has s1x_position/s1x_kelly, s2x_position/s2x_kelly and s1rf_* columns. Simulate them with _simulate_straddle_pnl and store in full_results.parquet. (7) Rename 'S1 (IVR Spread)' to 'S1 (PDV–IV spread)'. (8) Rerun and regenerate data_store/backtest/full_results.parquet/.pkl.

Rename the 'S1 IVR' labels (lines ~287, 367, 502) to 'S1 PDV–IV', since no implied-vol rank exists. Optionally add regime_forward_premium_table(spx, vix) and regime_label_summary(labels) from regime_classifier to the report, so the regime premise and persistence baseline are checked on every run.

(1) Lines ~302 and ~359: replace the hard-coded '63.4%' with clf.metadata_['evaluation']['oos_acc'] (0.751) and show persistence_acc (0.868) from the same dict; update the comment at ~277-278. The shipped pickle is a new version-robust format and pickle.load still works; predict_proba is holdout-calibrated. (2) Live inference reads d['pdv_forecast'] before the PDV block sets it, so pdv_iv_spread = −VIX; compute the PDV block first. (3) _refresh_regime_labels: drop clf.predict and pdv_model.pkl, and write rule labels via regime_classifier.build_rule_label_frame(spx, vix), which gives same-day FEATURE_COLS + rv_20d + vvix_gate + regime. (4) Improvements step 5: the backtest now uses the adaptive gate too. R2 share in the 2018-01..2025-03 window is 48.1% fixed vs 23.4% adaptive; full 2010-2026 is 32.6% vs 22.4% (not '~53% → ~25%'). Step 6: 'holdout isotonic (calibrated on 2018-19 rows the booster never saw); OOS P(R2) ECE 0.150 → 0.031'. (5) Persistence baseline on the page should be regime_label_summary(labels, '2020-01-01', '2025-12-31') on the displayed labels (86.7%), not 90.0%. (6) Variants table: use the engine's simulated s1x/s2x columns (see backtest request). (7) 'S1 IVR' labels at ~986 and ~1011.

Line ~331: the persistence baseline literal 90.0% should be 86.7% (adaptive labels, 2020-2025), preferably templated. Lines ~170 and ~339-341: replace the 63.4% / 86.2% / 90% narrative with the computed numbers (OOS 75.1% vs persistence 86.8%; with vvix 72.3%; with vvix + lag 83.1%) and drop 'circular vvix', since lagged vvix is a legitimate predictor. Regime legend 'R0 Low VIX / backwardation → buy straddles' is wrong: R0 has the HIGHER mean VIX (0.187 vs R1 0.167) and only 4.4% of R0 days are in backwardation. Use 'R0: trailing realised above implied (descriptive)'.

Lines ~381 and ~405-406: update '86.2%', '63.4% vs 90.0%' and 'loses by 27 points' to OOS 75.1% vs persistence 86.8% (gap 11.7 pp). Lines ~73, 273, 614: rename 'IVR' to 'PDV–IV'. Update the S2 stop description: the stop is now a 15% VIX move against the straddle held.

Optional: extend_regime_labels can call regime_classifier.build_rule_label_frame(spx, vix) to get same-day features and labels in one call. vvix_threshold=None remains correct and equals R2_GATE. Update the docstring's '63.4% ... 90.0%' to the computed numbers (75.1% vs 86.8%).

Regenerate from build_rule_label_frame(spx, vix) (owner: ops/dashboard). Rule labels changed on 2021-05-20 (a missing VVIX print is now carried forward: 1 → 2). The 47 adaptive-gate warm-up sessions 2010-01-26..2010-04-02 are now unlabelled. The feature columns, NaN before 2026-06-22, can be backfilled with real same-day values. The C21 test (adaptive vs shipped > 99% agreement) still passes on the current file (99.98%).

The regime_labels table holds classifier predictions with t−1 features under date t and rv_20d = 2·VIX − RV. Regenerate it with regime_classifier._write_labels_to_db(build_rule_label_frame(spx, vix)), which writes rule labels with same-day VIX, slope and rv_20d and confidence 1.0, or drop the table (get_regime_labels has no callers).
Docstring line ~17 'R2 (VOMMA_ACTIVE, VVIX > 100)': the R2 gate is now the adaptive rolling 252-session 80th percentile of VVIX (regime_classifier.R2_GATE).

Docs stage: see published_number_changes. Also rename 'IVR' (README:35,157; substack:22). The S3 'long dispersion (short index vol)' description contradicts the code: +1 is a bet that VIX/VVIX reverts up, which the P&L proxy pays and the combiner counts as long index vol.

api_changes:
regime_classifier.py:
NEW: R2_GATE (None = adaptive), R2_GATE_WINDOW / R2_GATE_QUANTILE / R2_GATE_MIN_PERIODS, VVIX_FFILL_LIMIT, fill_vvix(), r2_gate_threshold(vvix, thr=R2_GATE), r2_gate_state(), gate_name(), build_rule_label_frame(spx, vix, thr=R2_GATE, pdv_vol_series=None), regime_label_summary(labels, start, end), regime_forward_premium_table(spx, vix, labels=None, horizon=21), regime_label_db_rows(frame), classifier_accuracy_report(spx, vix, pdv_vol_series=None, ...), SHIPPED_FIT_KWARGS, TEST_END_DATE, CLASSIFIER_PREDICTIONS_PARQUET, PDV_SOURCE_* tags, HMMRegimeClassifier.map_states_to_regimes().

BEHAVIOUR / DEFAULT CHANGES:
- vvix_threshold now defaults to R2_GATE (adaptive; was 100.0) in build_regime_labels, build_dataset, train_classifier, RegimePipeline and regime_label_noise_audit. Pass 100.0 explicitly to reproduce the old labels.
- Labels drop sessions whose gate state is unknown (adaptive warm-up, VVIX outage longer than 1 session).
- build_dataset and train_classifier gained pdv_vol_series; train_classifier gained feature_cols and fit_kwargs.
- RegimeClassifier.fit(X, y, use_sample_weights=True, calibration=None|'holdout', calibration_frac=0.2): the default no longer wraps an in-sample isotonic model. model_ is an xgb.XGBClassifier; new attributes calibration_ and metadata_; new pickle format with legacy pickles still loading.
- evaluate_classifier(..., labels=None) adds persistence_n, n_test, test_window, feature_cols, r2_gate, pdv_iv_spread_source.
- save_regime_labels defaults to regime_classifier_predictions.parquet with columns pred_regime / pred_regime_name, and raises on the rule-label path.
- RegimePipeline(pdv_model_path=None, pdv_vol_series=None): no full-sample PDV by default.
- _write_labels_to_db(label_frame) writes rule labels.
- HMMRegimeClassifier uses filtered inference, n_init=5 and log_likelihood_, and requires n_components == 3.
- build_features: .attrs provenance; pdv_vol_series validated (ValueError on vol points or negatives); vvix carries one missing print.
- regime_label_noise_audit returns an r2_gate key.

signal_engine.py:
- SignalEngine.generate no longer modifies precomputed_regimes; it only lags them by one session.
- It keeps sessions with NaN features, computes trailing statistics on all supplied history and allows entries only inside the window.
- New output columns: s1x_*, s2x_*, s2_z, s2x_z, s3_z, s4_z, s2_stop, s2x_stop. New .attrs: regime_source, pdv_iv_spread_source, n_sessions_dropped.
- _run_statemachine and _run_statemachine_r2exit gained optional exit_long, exit_short and entry_allowed; every generate_signal* gained optional entry_allowed.
- New S1_EXIT_BAND. S2_STOP_LOSS_PCT now means a 15% VIX move against the straddle.
- combine_signals(..., max_kelly=None).
- signal_summary key 'Signal1_IVR' renamed to 'Signal1_PDV_IV'.
- SIGNALS_PATH removed; use default_signals_path(df).
- signal_engine no longer imports VVIX_REGIME2_THRESHOLD.

SIGNAL-SIDE SUPPORT FOR EXCLUDED FINDINGS:
- signals-s3-mechanical-zscore-pnl: sig_df['s3_z'] exposes S3's lagged decision z. The backtest's P&L z (_build_s3_zscore) is same-day and should stay so, with its 'matches exactly' claim reworded.
- signals-variants-table-fabricated: sig_df now carries s1x_position/kelly, s2x_position/kelly and s1rf_* to simulate with _simulate_straddle_pnl.
- signals-app-refresh-writes-classifier-labels and signals-live-pdv-percentile-nan: build_rule_label_frame gives same-day features plus rule labels for any history, for the dashboard refresh and the feature backfill.
- Dashboard accuracy display: RegimeClassifier.load().metadata_['evaluation'] provides oos_acc, persistence_acc, n_test, test_window and P(R2) ECE/Brier.
- PDV hook for the horizon-21 forecast: build_features(pdv_vol_series=σ̂) and SignalEngine.generate(precomputed_pdv_vol=σ̂). The contract is annualised decimal σ at the VIX horizon (~21 sessions), dated ≤ t (walk-forward). BacktestEngine._build_walkforward_pdv_vol is the single place to swap it in.

test_result: 1 failed, 708 passed, 24 skipped, 4 warnings in 159.11s. The one failure is the non-owned test_backtest_engine.py::TestEdgeCases::test_all_regime2_no_s1_entries: a constant VVIX=150 is not R2 under the adaptive gate. This is an intended behaviour change; the suggested fix is verified and listed in cross_chain_requests.
notes_for_integration:
Branch c22/signals, 5 commits on 3462e2c. The worktree is clean. Committed artifacts: re-trained data_store/signals/regime_classifier.pkl (new version-robust format) and the deletion of data_store/signals/signals_2015_2025.parquet and data_store/ivr_spread_panel.parquet. regime_labels.parquet and vol_system.db are not touched and need regeneration by their owners.

1. Merge order: this chain changes the default R2 gate. The backtest picks it up through build_regime_labels(spx, vix) with no code change in backtest_engine.py, so every backtest number moves (NAV 738,794 → 444,614 with signal fixes only). Rerun the backtest after the PDV and backtest chains merge. My numbers isolate the signals-side deltas with WF PDV and P&L code unchanged.

2. The full suite has one expected failure, test_backtest_engine.py::TestEdgeCases::test_all_regime2_no_s1_entries (not mine). Its constant-VVIX premise is invalid under the adaptive gate. Fix: VVIX = np.linspace(80, 200, n), verified to give 100% R2 and 0 combined activity.

3. The test count rose from the 642 baseline to 708 passed (+66 new or strengthened tests in the three owned test files).

4. Performance note: with n_jobs=-1, XGBoost was pathologically slow on this oversubscribed machine (load 40-50 on 4 cores): a 0.5 s fit took over 15 minutes. I ran heavy jobs with OMP_NUM_THREADS=1; no code change. The shipped pickle was produced by train_classifier defaults (data as_of 2025-12-31 from 2010; adaptive labels; rv-proxy pdv_iv_spread; no vvix; balanced weights; holdout isotonic). Its metadata_['evaluation'] reads oos_acc 0.7513, persistence 0.8676 (1,488 rows), P(R2) ECE 0.150 → 0.031. R2 recall is 0.278; both stress dates (2020-03-16, 2025-04-09) are predicted R2.

5. Classifier numbers for the docs stage, all on adaptive labels: in-sample 78.7%, OOS 75.1%, per-year walk-forward 75.1%, persistence 86.8%; benchmarks with vvix 72.3% OOS and with vvix + lag 83.1%. Fixed-100 labels for reference: OOS 52.6% vs persistence 91.1%. Script: scratchpad/work-signals/clf_report.py.

6. Mutation testing: 17/17 mutations caught by the owned tests (scratchpad/work-signals/mutate.py, mut_results.txt). Running the new test modules against the old code fails at import (the new APIs are missing).

7. Scripts for reproduction live in scratchpad/work-signals/: bt_run.py and bt_decomp.py for backtest attribution, cmp_labels.py, retrain_shipped.py and bt_repro.py.

8. No pip dependencies were added. hmmlearn is still optional (imported inside fit/test). scipy.stats.multivariate_normal is used for the HMM filter; scipy is already in requirements.

9. The S2 stop constant keeps its value (0.15) but now means a 15% VIX move against the straddle held, not 15% of slope.

10. The dashboard can pickle.load the new classifier and call predict_proba on its 6-column frame. Probabilities can be exactly 0 (isotonic).
